fusar_both_attrs.hd5.description: elevation_limits and range both present: elevation_limits wins

fusar_bytes_attrs.hd5.description: attributes stored as fixed-length byte strings (h5py returns numpy bytes)

fusar_no_attrs.hd5.description: no z attributes: default z range [0, shape[-1] - 1]

fusar_numeric_attrs.hd5.description: numeric (not string) attributes: eval() raises TypeError in the original

fusar_one_key_range.hd5.description: one key, float32, range attribute only, no pixel spacings

fusar_three_keys.hd5.description: three keys: the importer always takes key index 1 (b_tomogram)

fusar_two_key_elev.hd5.description: two keys (theta, tomogram), complex64, elevation_limits on the dataset, ps_az and ps_rg strings on the file

npy_complex_nan_inf.npy.description: complex64 with NaN, +inf and -inf samples, one azimuth-range line all NaN

npy_covariance_5d.npy.description: 5-D 3x3 covariance-like cube; TomoVis keeps sqrt of the diagonal as 3 channels

npy_one_range_line.npy.description: shape[-1] == 1: the slice slider stays at 0 and nothing is drawn on load

rat_complex.rat.description: complex64 RAT 2.0 file written by ste_io.srat (1000-byte header, C-order payload)

uavsar_three_keys.h5.description: three keys (lat, lon, tomo); the importer takes key index 2 and applies np.rollaxis(x, 1, 0)
